summary: Frontend-only regression run after the useCallback/stable-key refactor. Verified QuizPage (list, open, full answer+submit, deep-link /quiz/{id}), IdeasPage (list, Teacher's Picks, sort/category refetch, share idea + badge toasts, like), LeaderboardPage (student rows + age/subject filters, teacher tabs), ChatPage (conversations, debounced user search, send message, 5s polling keeps thread), ContestsPage (list, detail, join, full contest quiz render 5 questions x 4 options, submit + ranking), ContentHub (areas, content list, tab filters, detail dialog body + Show Solution), Student dashboard (stats, weekly recap, badges grid 12 tiles, announcements + mark-read, today's challenges + Mark Done with points update, certificates), Teacher dashboard (stats, verified badge, create daily challenge, create contest, announcements create + read counter + cancel/confirm delete, my students/challenges/contests). Explicitly instrumented every page with a network-request counter: no infinite refetch loops anywhere - every fetcher fires exactly twice on mount (React StrictMode double-invoke in dev) and exactly once per filter change; idle periods produce zero extra requests except the intended 5s chat poll. No console errors observed on any page.

integration_issues.flow: Student dashboard first load - badge count in 'Ideas & Awards' card
integration_issues.issue: Badges are granted lazily by GET /api/badges, while GET /api/stats/me runs in parallel, so on the very first load after a new badge is earned the stat card can show '0/12 badges' while the My Badges card shows '3/12'. Self-corrects on next load/refresh. Cosmetic data-freshness inconsistency, not caused by the refactor.

issues: Rows for users without an age_group render a dangling label '@Efon • Ages' (empty age group). Should hide the 'Ages' text when age_group is missing.

action_items: Optional: hide the 'Ages' suffix on leaderboard rows when a user has no age_group.
Optional: have /api/stats/me evaluate badge grants (or refresh stats after BadgesCard load) so the badge count in the stat card is never one load behind.

Optional code-quality (eslint, non-blocking): react/no-unstable-nested-components in ChatPage.js:95, ContentHub.js:58, Navbar.js:25 (nested component definitions re-created each render - the same class of issue this refactor targeted), plus ~20 react/no-unescaped-entities warnings.
critical_code_review_comments: QuizPage deep-link effect ([id, quizzes, startQuiz]) is safe: startQuiz is a stable useCallback([]) and quizzes only changes on fetch, so the quiz auto-starts exactly once - verified with request counters (1 /api/quizzes call per mount pair, question counter stayed at 'Question 1 of 5' during a 6s idle).

IdeasPage fetchIdeas useCallback([API, sort, category]) triggers exactly one /api/ideas refetch per filter change; fetchSpotlights depends only on API so it does not refetch on filter change - correct.
ChatPage 5s poll re-fetches the open thread without remounting or clearing messages; sent message stayed rendered after 9s of polling.

context_for_next_testing_agent: No functional regressions from the hook/key refactor. Pattern that produced false negatives in my first pass: waiting only for the card wrapper testid (e.g. student-announcements-card, daily-challenges-card) returns 0 children because those cards render before their fetch resolves - add an explicit wait/timeout (~3-4s) or wait for a child selector. Note teststudent has already attempted contest 779c1d56, so use sam_patel/maya_r when a fresh contest attempt is needed. Contest option testids are contest-q{qi}-option-{oi}; chat search input is chat-search-input and results are chat-partner-{username}; students can only search teachers ('sarah').
rca_of_the_issue: No loop/stale-data regression found. Request counters showed the expected 2x-on-mount (StrictMode) and 1x-per-filter-change behaviour for /api/quizzes, /api/ideas, /api/ideas/spotlights, /api/leaderboard/*, /api/content, /api/tournaments, /api/announcements, /api/challenges/*, /api/badges. The single data inconsistency (badge count in stat card) is a backend read-ordering artefact (badge grants happen inside GET /api/badges), pre-existing and cosmetic.
